newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Croatia kicks off roadshow for 2nd Eurobond issue.
newsitem.headline: Croatia kicks off roadshow for 2nd Eurobond issue.

text.p: Croatia kicked off a roadshow for the country's second Eurobond issue on Thursday in Vienna, hoping to tap into Austria's largely retail-oriented investor base to help fund economic reconstruction.

The 700 million schilling issue by Croatia's Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR) is guaranteed by the Republic of Croatia and primarily aimed at helping to finance the modernisation of the country's sprawling tourism industry.

The five-year issue will be priced next week at 80 basis points over the interpolated five-year Austrian bond yield curve and listed in Vienna and Luxembourg, lead manager Creditanstalt-Bankverein said in a statement.
Croatia is rated at the bottom of the investment grade ladder, carrying a Baa3 from Moody's and a BBB- from Standard & Poors.
The country made its debut on the Eurobond market earlier this year with a $250 million issue.
The government plans a further issue, to be denominated in German marks, in the second half of the year.
"We're already having very serious discussions with our lead managers," Finance Minister Bozo Prka told a news briefing in Vienna. He declined to be drawn on the size of the planned issue.
